ADDITIONAL KNOWLEDGE / SKILLS • Health Sciences, Life Sciences, Pharmacy or Nursing degree preferred, or Sr.CRA and/or ACRP Certification/Designation. • Experience with Phase I–IV clinical trials is preferred. • Thorough knowledge of ICH-GCP and local regulatory requirements. • Proficient in using EDC systems (e.g., Medidata Rave, Oracle InForm), IRT, eTMF, CTMS, and Microsoft Office Suite. • Ability to travel up to 40-60%, depending on project assignment and geographic location of sites. • Strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills; able to work independently and within cross-functional teams. • Great communication and organizational skills, detailed orientation and sense of urgency are required. • Holder of a valid driver’s license. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us. (€3,000 ) Additionally: Annual Bonus (Short Term Incentive Program) target = 8% of annual salary A monthly stipend of €157.83 (pro-rated based on hours of work), to be paid with their regular payroll/added to their taxable income. review_candidates.title: Social Services Manager
review_candidates.description: Who We Are International Justice Mission (IJM) is a global leader in protecting vulnerable people from violence around the world. Our team of over 1,200 professionals are at work worldwide in over 30 offices. Together we are on a mission to rescue millions, protect half a billion, and make justice unstoppable. We are a global community that cares for one another. We believe that the way we work is as important as the results we achieve. We provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve. The Need For over 25 years, IJM has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, IJM’s Justice System Strengthening Projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50 and 85% for very large populations of people in poverty. As we grow to expand our impact to protect 500 million people from violence, we are seeking a Social Services Manager, will be responsible for the development and execution of the Aftercare vision and strategy for the portfolio of IJM Bangladesh. Social Services Manager, Bangladesh will equip IJM multi-disciplinary teams to deliver strategies that ensure that trauma-informed justice systems and social services empower trafficking survivors toward restoration. The position will build Aftercare expertise at the regional level that advises stakeholders, builds innovative partnerships, and establishes best practices for Aftercare programming to combat the internal Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children (CSEC). He/she will produce standard quality products, and training for IJM field offices and partners. The position will liaise with the Regional Justice Solutions team and the Divisonal Directors (Dhaka, Khulna, mymensingh and Barisal) to share best practice, align on shared initiatives, and consult on data priorities to develop evidence-based Aftercare models of implementation. Social Services Manager, Bangladesh will also provide case management consultation to ensure the highest quality aftercare is provided to IJM clients; provide professional development training to increase IJM staff capacity and leadership; facilitate and support aftercare partnership development to ensure a strong network of sufficient and quality local aftercare services; advise on aftercare-related system reform and sustainability program development and implementation; and work with the Director, Justice System Program on strategy and program development, monitoring, evaluation and implementation. The role is based in Dhaka, but will provide support nationally, including travelling to each of IJM’s future program locations (Khulna, Barisal and Mymensingh). Responsibilities Strategy, Knowledge Development, & Implementation: In collaboration with the Regional Justice Solutions, Director of Dhaka and Khulna, facilitate process of developing and updating national Aftercare strategy for Bangladesh. Ensure that the design, development, and implementation of Aftercare programs under the CSEC program are aligned with IJM’s 2030 vision and IJM’s Global and Regional Aftercare strategies, including the Global Survivor Network. In coordination with the Regional Justice Solutions, Director of Program, Directors of Dhaka and Khulna, develop and implement tools, models of care, products, and resources for cross-border and source country programs that will result in more effective and sustainable interventions for survivors. Contribute to the national Aftercare program assessments, expansion, and partnership activation in Bangladesh, including support for proposals and program design as needed. Provide consultation and receive feedback on Aftercare casework and system reform activities, strategies, challenges, team development, and policy compliance. Remaining up to date on innovative trends and developments in Aftercare and Survivor support approaches globally and regionally through research, exposure/learning trips, and networking; propose enhancements or integration of best practices into existing IJM programs, including survivor voice and empowerment initiatives. Policies & Procedures Develop replicable policies, guidelines, best practices, and other processes related to Aftercare. Ensure that best practices and lessons learned on Aftercare development for trafficking in person are well documented. Networking & Partnership Establish and nurture cooperative relationships with the Directors of Dhaka and Khulna, Regional Justice Solution, South Asia, Aftercare professionals, organizations, and coalitions. Represent IJM’s internal CSEC Aftercare program in coalition and stakeholder meetings, conferences, and workshops. Communication Development of briefs, papers, fact sheets, and other communication resources as necessary that articulates IJM’s approach and strategy for Aftercare. Ensure knowledge sharing and lessons learned among IJM and other IJM regional Aftercare teams, promoting avenues for shared learnings and collaboration. Training And Development In collaboration with Aftercare and casework leaders, identify areas of internal capacity building needs for IJM Aftercare teams; develop resources and training or mentoring plans to equip teams with knowledge and skills necessary to effectively serve CSEC survivors. In collaboration with regional Aftercare leaders and teams, develop or adapt external capacity building training resources and curricula for CSEC Aftercare partners and service providers. Research, Program Management, And M&E In collaboration with the M&E team, support the data collection and analysis of Aftercare standardized indicators for anti-trafficking programs. Documentation, Reporting & Data Management Analyze and document cases of Trafficking of Human Beings (TBH) that can contribute to updated case management protocols. Research the issue of THB in Bangladesh as relevant for program development and goal setting for the IJM Bangladesh office. Work with Bangladesh National team members to monitor and evaluate the project, including monitoring and reporting of project targets, results, collection of data, and output delivery. Contribute to the timely submission of reports and monitoring progress for grant objectives. Casework Provide mentoring and support to social welfare officers and justice officials to ensure that survivors of THB are provided with trauma-informed protection and support throughout the investigation and court proceedings. Provide court preparation and support to survivors of THB. Provide mentoring and support to social welfare officers and other stakeholders to empower survivors of THB towards restoration by conducting holistic assessments to evaluate survivor strengths and vulnerabilities including the safety of the home and community environment, developing individualized care and safety plans and ensuring their implementation to address vulnerabilities and critical needs, coordinating psychosocial services for survivors, monitoring and reporting survivor progress towards defined psychosocial goals and assessing sustainable safety at the time of case closure; and Collaborate with police, social services department, shelter partners, other government bodies and team members to continually assess and implement safety and security plans. Qualifications Master’s degree in social work, psychology, or related field. Minimum five years of relevant experience working with survivors of trauma; clinical experience preferred, including provision of therapy. Minimum five years of experience in team management. Experience in networking and partnering with social service providers. Capacity to develop and deliver trainings in English and Bengali to government and non-governmental agency partners, on the topic of trauma, crisis intervention, methods of intervention adapted for survivors of trauma and trauma-informed casework, among other topics. Proficiency in the Microsoft Office Suite with the ability to quickly learn and consistently use other software systems for purposes of case management, M&E, and documentation. Preferred experience includes working nationally and on multi-disciplinary teams. Significant networking and advocacy experience required. Strong understanding of trauma and proven application of trauma-informed approaches within case management and/or clinical interventions. Proven ability to mentor, guide and coach multi-disciplinary stakeholders. Prior experience working with law enforcement or justice system officials preferred. Fluent in written and oral communication in Bengali and English. Excellent writing, documentation, and reporting skills, including the ability to maintain digital records and generate high-quality reports on all casework interventions, stakeholder interactions, etc. An advantage to ability to contribute or develop program proposals. Training and curriculum development. Research and writing. High level of proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and data management systems. Critical Qualities Multi-cultural awareness and competency. Passionate commitment to IJM’s mission and values including bridge building and professionalism. Servant leader, humble. Courageous, ability to think creatively and innovatively. Attention to detail, organized, and disciplined with priorities. Professional in demeanor, appearance, writing, and oral communication. Works well under stress with a sustained positive attitude. Exceptionally high levels of honesty and integrity. Intelligent, creative, and proactive problem solver. Diplomatic and flexible with strong service ethics. Ability to contribute outside of the designated areas of responsibility, team player. Other Duties The candidate should be willing to travel across Bangladesh and internationally for official purposes when needed. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. All positions are required to perform any additional tasks assigned by the supervisor Application Process Upload Resume & Cover Letter in one PDF document and send the application to bangladeshrecruitment@ijm.org. Candidate selection is based on technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring criteria subject to assessing the candidate's value congruence and thorough background, police clearance, and reference check processes.

Contexto del Proyecto En Costa Rica las acciones del PNUD tienen como objetivo principal la promoción del desarrollo y los derechos humanos, la protección del ambiente y el apoyo al país para lograr la inclusión social de todas las poblaciones del país, así como el fortalecimiento de su sistema democrático. Este enfoque implica una drástica modificación de los enfoques tradicionales del desarrollo, fuertemente ligados al logro del crecimiento económico. Esta visión tiene claros puntos de contacto con la experiencia costarricense en las últimas décadas, que le hace figurar hoy en la vanguardia del mundo en desarrollo en materia de bienestar para su población. La posición a contratar realizará funciones para dos proyectos de la cartera de PNUD Costa Rica: 1) la Iniciativa Finanzas para la Biodiversidad (BIOFIN) y 2) Fortalecimiento de la gestión de riesgos ambientales y sociales con énfasis en naturaleza en el Sistema de Banca para el Desarrollo (SBD). Por su parte, La Iniciativa Finanzas para la Biodiversidad (BIOFIN) fue lanzada por el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) en el 2012 como una nueva alianza mundial para abordar el desafío de la financiación de la biodiversidad de una manera integral, bajo la premisa que la inversión en biodiversidad es inversión en desarrollo sostenible. Frente a la múltiple crisis que enfrenta la humanidad, BIOFIN ofrece soluciones y mecanismos financieros concretos hacia una recuperación económica más verde, inclusiva y resiliente. BIOFIN se desarrolla en 132 países del mundo, entre ellos destaca Costa Rica quien ha sido pionero y promotor de la iniciativa desde 2012. La visión de BIOFIN Costa Rica es promover y entregar mecanismos financieros para reducir y contener una brecha creciente para el financiamiento de la biodiversidad con al menos USD 100 millones de recursos movilizados / catalizados. Esta meta financiera equivale a 5 años de brecha financiera (en un escenario optimista) estimada en USD 20 millones anuales. La principal diversificación de las fuentes de financiamiento incluirá mecanismos que mejoren la participación del sector privado / financiero. BIOFIN Ofrece 7 Soluciones Financieras (SF) Concretas e Innovadoras y Un Componente Transversal De Integración De Igualdad De Género, Para Movilizar Recursos Para Que Costa Rica Pueda Aumentar y Hacer Más Efectiva y Eficiente La Inversión En La Conservación, El Uso Sostenible y La Distribución Equitativa De Los Beneficios De Los Ecosistemas y La Biodiversidad. Dichas Soluciones Financieras Incluyen Fortalecimiento de las finanzas, eficiencia y capacidades del sistema nacional de conservación. Plataforma de Concesiones de Servicios y Actividades No Esenciales. Nueva Generación del Pago por Servicios Ambientales. Alianzas Público-Privadas: Crowdfunding Huella del Futuro. Capital Semilla y Empresarialidad para el Turismo Sostenible. Plataforma de Financiamiento de Bionegocios. Alineamiento de flujos naturaleza-positivos en el sector financiero. Asimismo, BIOFIN Desarrolla Análisis Que Permitan Entender Mejor Los Desafíos y Oportunidades Frente Al Financiamiento De La Biodiversidad, Desarrollando Herramientas Que Permitan Visibilizar La Importancia Del Capital Natural En Costa Rica, El Gasto Público Vinculado a La Biodiversidad, La Brecha De Financiamiento De La Biodiversidad, Mismos Que Son La Base Para Desarrollar Un Plan De Financiamiento Para La Biodiversidad Que Busca Reducir La Brecha De Recursos Financieros a Partir De La generación de nuevas fuentes de ingresos, Mejorar la efectividad y eficiencia de los existentes, Evitar costos futuros, y Diversificar fuentes de financiamiento Asimismo, el proyecto Fortalecimiento de la gestión de riesgos ambientales y sociales con énfasis en naturaleza en el Sistema de Banca para el Desarrollo (SBD) es una iniciativa que propone el desarrollo e implementación de un Sistema de Administración de Riesgos Ambientales y Sociales (SARAS) integrado con el marco de divulgación del Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD), adaptado a las características operativas del SBD. Esta integración permitirá identificar, evaluar, gestionar y divulgar de forma estructurada los riesgos y oportunidades relacionados con la naturaleza, incorporando el enfoque LEAP del TNFD y el principio de doble materialidad, que considera tanto los impactos de la naturaleza sobre las instituciones como los impactos de estas sobre la naturaleza. La estrategia de dicho proyecto se implementará en cuatro fases: diagnóstico y análisis de sensibilidad, diseño metodológico, implementación progresiva y divulgación alineada con estándares internacionales. A lo largo de estas fases se generarán productos clave como una política de sostenibilidad actualizada, herramientas digitales, esquemas de gobernanza, procesos de capacitación y reportes de divulgación.
